## Observed at the current default commit

Current main `39cb4a46d76ec4c154bfc7719ded9d7a10985fc0`, freshly rechecked November 4, 2026, 00:55 UTC. The [release job](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rl/actions/runs/41712831531/job/126185066858) timed out waiting for protected release [PR #139](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rl/pull/139) on November 3. This report concerns the reason/remedy it printed, not the merge protection or the timeout itself.

The exact job log records successful approval of [CI run 41736191361](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rl/actions/runs/41736191361) at 23:05:02 UTC. Bun release (26) began at 23:27:25 UTC, before the release timeout at 23:34:57 UTC. Yet the terminal error says the PR did not merge because CI is awaiting workflow approval and asks the maintainer to approve it once. The checks were already allowed to execute. Other checks could still be queued or running; this does not claim all required checks passed by the deadline.

## Exact source evidence and goal

- [Initialization](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rl/blob/39cb4a46d76ec4c154bfc7719ded9d7a10985fc0/.github/workflows/release.yml#L286) sets `awaiting_approval=0` once before the polling loop.
- [Run discovery and approval](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rl/blob/39cb4a46d76ec4c154bfc7719ded9d7a10985fc0/.github/workflows/release.yml#L397-L411) queries current approval-waiting runs, attempts approval, then sets `awaiting_approval=1`. It never clears the historical flag on subsequent empty observations or a successful approval.
- [Deadline diagnostic](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rl/blob/39cb4a46d76ec4c154bfc7719ded9d7a10985fc0/.github/workflows/release.yml#L416) selects the approval-specific error from that latched flag, rather than current run state. The diagnostic can therefore contradict the job's own successful-approval evidence.
- The nearby workflow comments explicitly intend to make the merge wait diagnosable and surface an actual required maintainer action. The existing [release goal](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rl/blob/39cb4a46d76ec4c154bfc7719ded9d7a10985fc0/.agents/pm/issues/pm-rl-wlj0.toon) preserves protected metadata merge and explicit release gates. This request retains those protections.

Expected: at timeout, distinguish a current approval block from checks already queued/running, with a remedy backed by the current observation. Actual: any earlier approval wait permanently selects a stale approval remedy.

Impact: release triage asks the maintainer to perform a completed action and hides the actual remaining check/merge wait. No publication, tagging, permission change or bypass is requested; the job states nothing was published/tagged.

## Regression criteria

1. Derive the timeout reason from fresh run/check state; distinguish unknown/API failure from a known approval block.
2. Cover approval-required → approved → queued/running across multiple polls, including successful approval in the final iteration. The terminal result must not request another approval.
3. Keep an actionable approval URL when a run truly remains blocked; retain generic/current check diagnostics otherwise.
4. Preserve the 30-minute bound, protected merge, explicit release gate, publication/tag sequencing and fail-closed behavior. Do not loosen permissions or required checks.

## Scope and duplicate check

Read-only exact hosted logs, current workflow source and run/job timestamps; no workflow rerun, local full-suite claim, provider call or release action. Workflow bytes were verified against their Git blob identity. Checked 139 all-status GitHub issues/PRs and 123 canonical tracker records, plus the release PR's issue comments, inline comments and reviews. Existing release-readiness and protected-publish-order work does not own this stale diagnostic. Similar findings in other packages do not fix this repository's copied workflow.
Release timeout retains an approval warning after CI was successfully approved
